conviction_note: Q4 itself is the base case (consensus $2.50 / $1.13bn sits near the top of the quarter the FY26 guide implies, and Woodward has beaten four straight); the move turns on the first FY27 guide against a street at $10.75 EPS / $4.72bn, which the company's own stated headwinds (pricing from ~8% to 3-5%, China on-highway gone, aftermarket decelerating, fuel/geopolitics 'felt in FY27') and TransDigm's below-street FY27 guide make hard to clear at the midpoint. Against that, the stock has already de-rated ~16% from its post-Q3 high, short interest is ~2% of float, and Woodward's last first-guide (Nov 2025, conservative $7.50-8.00) was bought +12.4%. So p_up 46 on a 10% absolute move gives -0.8; the findings sum to -1.0, the two measurements agree in sign and size.

The bar the stock trades on is the FY27 guide: street FY27 EPS $10.75 (+13.4%) and revenue $4.72bn (+8.8%) per stockanalysis.com (13 analysts, S&P Global), single aggregator source.

next_guide.company_current_guide: none for FY27; Blankenship on 2026-07-29 called it 'a little premature' and gave no number, deferring long-term questions to an Investor Day on 2027-03-04 (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978089-20260808). next_guide.basis: First FY27 guide arrives with this print; the company itself named pricing normalising from ~8% to 3-5%, China on-highway ending (~$40m/quarter, ~90bp of Industrial margin), and geopolitics/fuel affecting aftermarket in FY27, TransDigm guided FY27 aftermarket to high single digits and EPS below street on 2026-11-10, and Woodward's last first-guide (FY26, $7.50-8.00) ended ~20% below where the year finished — so the initial guide is more likely to sit below the $10.75 street midpoint than above it.

findings.finding: The first FY27 guide lands against a street of $10.75 EPS (+13.4% on FY26 ~$9.48) and $4.72bn revenue (+8.8%), while management's own July statements set up a slower year: company-wide pricing ~10% in Q3 (incl. a ~100bp one-time retro aero adjustment) and ~8% for FY26 normalising to '3-5%' going forward, China on-highway ($40m in Q3, ~90bp of Industrial margin) 'no significant' sales from Q4, no FY27 number given; Woodward's last initial guide (FY26 $7.50-8.00) was raised four times to $9.30-9.50, i.e. it guides conservatively — so a midpoint below $10.75 is the more likely print, partly offset by the market having de-rated the stock for exactly this.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025 print with the conservative initial FY26 guide ($7.50-8.00): +12.44% next session (baseline 2025-11-24). July 2026 beat-and-raise sold -7.56% / -13.9% on the week on FY27 setup (China exit, pricing). Feb 2026 guide raise +13.42%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is ~16% below its post-Q3 high and below the 200-day, but sell-side targets (mean $420.5, low $380) and the FY27 EPS estimate ($10.75, +13%) have not come down to a pricing-normalised, China-less year; if the street had absorbed the July commentary FY27 EPS would sit nearer the low $10s and targets would have been cut.
findings.independence: Street figures from a different source: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/wwd/forecast/ (2026-11-02). Conservative-guide habit: https://www.woodward.com/press-release/woodward-reports-strong-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-results (FY26 guide raised from $7.5-8.0, 2026-02-02). Counter-evidence (Nov 2025 conservative guide bought +12.4%) is the reason this is sized small.

findings.finding: TransDigm (2026-11-10) guided FY27 commercial aftermarket to high-single-digit growth from 14% in FY26, OEM to HSD-LDD from ~15%, defense HSD from 10%, cited weaker RPKs on elevated oil and Middle East tension, and guided EPS midpoint ~$47.52 below the $48.66 consensus; shares fell ~4% premarket.
findings.link: Same end market and same buyers: both sell proprietary components and spares into commercial aftermarket and OEM airframes/engines; Woodward commercial services was $268m of $1,110m Q3 sales (24%), commercial OEM $234m (21%). TDG is a peer supplier, not a customer/supplier of WWD; it is the closest FY27 read on the same aftermarket.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: WWD fell -7.56% after the July print on forward-setup worries; commercial services growth has slowed 50% to 36% to 24% over three quarters (Earnings Whispers).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced into the sector: ITA fell 5% in the 5 days into WWD's print, matching WWD. What is not yet priced is whether Woodward's own FY27 aftermarket assumption follows TDG's deceleration; WWD's street FY27 revenue +8.8% assumes some deceleration already.
findings.independence: https://finviz.com/news/420228/transdigm-shares-fall-4-as-fy2027-earnings-outlook-misses-estimates-despite-q4-revenue-growth (same event, different write-up); Woodward's own Q2 call flagged geopolitical impact on aftermarket 'felt in fiscal 2027' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/04/29/woodward-wwd-q2-2026-earnings-transcript/, snippet_only).

findings.finding: GE Aerospace Q3 2026 (2026-10-20): commercial services +23%, internal shop-visit revenue +12%, LEAP shop visits +40%+, spare parts +20%+, 2026 guide raised (EPS $8.00-8.10 from $7.65-7.85), and 2027 commercial services guided to low-double-digit growth; stock fell ~9% in the week on jet-fuel/airline-profit worries tied to the Iran war.
findings.link: Woodward supplies fuel systems and controls on GE/CFM engines including LEAP; GE shop visits drive Woodward LRU/spares demand. Share of WWD revenue from GE not stated in sources.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: WWD commercial services +24% in Q3 FY26; CFO said LRU activity in Q4 would come down somewhat from Q3 'more like the first half'.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a month; supports a solid Sept quarter for Woodward aftermarket and an LDD (not HSD) 2027 shop-visit backdrop, which is above TDG's view. The market sold GE on fuel, not on the services number, so the volume read-through to WWD's Q4 is not the part being discounted.
findings.independence: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/23/why-ge-aerospace-stock-keeps-going-down/ (stock reaction and fuel concern). Partly opposes the TDG and Safran findings; kept separate because it is a different counterparty's number.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: WWD commercial services growth decelerated 50% to 36% to 24% over three quarters (Earnings Whispers 2026-11-11).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced as a sector deceleration; filed because it is a same-quarter counterparty showing the aftermarket deceleration Woodward's FY27 guide will have to assume.

findings.finding: Hexcel (2026-10-22) beat EPS by a penny but held its 2026 guide and fell 11.8% intraday; Woodward fell 6.2% the same day against ITA -0.6%, showing the market punishes aero suppliers at high multiples that hold rather than raise.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: WWD's own July beat-and-raise was sold -7.56%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a statement about the reaction function, not news: the market sells 'in line' aero guides. Already visible in WWD's price, which is why it is small.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-16 Woodward announced leadership changes effective 2027-01-01: COO Tom Cromwell moves to EVP Strategic Initiatives and the COO post 'will not be backfilled', Industrial president Randy Hobbs becomes Chief Transformation Officer (Lean), and an Aerospace EMSE GM takes over Industrial; no outlook statement. The stock fell 5.8% that day against ITA -2.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 16 -5.77% (sector -2.5%) on the day of release.
findings.why_not_priced: Already priced in the day's underperformance; the only unpriced element is whether the call reveals the change is tied to an Industrial reset (new Industrial lead two days before the FY27 guide). No document says so.

findings.finding: Expectations: WWD is ~16% below its post-Q3 high (~$383) and below its 200-day (~$364), trades at $321 against a mean target of $420.5 and a LOW target of $380, short interest is only ~1.8% of float, and the 5-day slide into the print (-5.0%) matched ITA exactly — the de-rating for FY27 headwinds is in the price while the sell-side numbers are not, so an FY27 guide merely near consensus would clear a lower real bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 (+13.42%) and Nov 2025 (+12.44%) prints came off weaker setups and were bought hard; July 2026 came off near-record highs and was sold.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the measure of what is priced: a 30% gap to mean target with every target above spot says the street has not cut, while the price has. If the guide disappoints, target cuts follow; if it is in line, the gap supports relief. Low short interest means the relief is not a squeeze but holders not selling.
findings.independence: Targets and street: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/wwd/forecast/; short interest: https://equibles.com/stocks/wwd/shortinterest; price path: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/ITA?range=1mo&interval=1d

findings.finding: FCF: guide $300-350m unchanged despite EPS raises; YTD FCF $196m with capex $156m against a ~$290m FY capex target, so Q4 needs capex of ~$134m (more than double Q3's $60m) and Q4 operating cash flow of ~$240-290m versus $352m in the first nine months; receivables and inventory have been rising.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FCF -12% was noted in post-print coverage of the July selloff (Webull 'stronger earnings masking growing strains in FCF').
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is visible in the Q3 release and flagged in the Earnings Whispers preview, so mostly priced; a miss on FCF or a weak FY27 FCF guide would add to a soft guide day.
findings.independence: https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/WWD/23144 (capex must more than double in Q4). Shares the Q3 release with the consensus_bar finding but a different line.

findings.finding: Capital return: $553m repurchased in the first nine months of FY26 and management expects ~$700m total returned for the year (implying ~$90m in Q4), at 1.6x debt/EBITDA with room for strategic moves.
findings.why_not_priced: Already guided; worth roughly zero unless an FY27 buyback figure surprises.

baseline_tension: The baseline gives no usable skew and a thin put-heavy chain; the sourced evidence leans mildly negative on the FY27 guide while the 26.7% drawdown from the 52-week high and targets far above spot argue that much of it is priced, so the lean is kept near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 3 (own caveat): the FY27-guide finding's own counter-evidence (conservative Nov 2025 first guide bought +12.4%) moved it from -1.5 to -1.2.
Rule 1 (this name sells beats): the Q4 consensus-beat finding from +0.3 to +0.2.
Rule 5 (proxy): Caterpillar power-gen read-through is a proxy with no named customer link, from +0.7 to +0.5.

Pessimism artefact: p_up moved from 45 to 46; abs_move_pct raised from 9.5 to 10.0 for a first FY27 guide (core table, guidance row). impact_sum unchanged at -1.0 because the three edits net to zero; scaled number -0.95 to -0.8.
